items.item: The six exterior sheets retain one body and component design, with corresponding A/B viewing angles and unchanged part-to-material assignments.
A and B use their specified accents over the shared base, retain R1 identification, and both dusk depictions show the closed/stowed mechanism state.
Both layouts, four interiors and two facilities sheets agree on fixed seating, tip-up geometry, passenger envelopes, doorway/bridge positions and support/control installations.
Matching A/B interior and facilities views retain geometry and material assignments while applying the named palette; corresponding mode views preserve the same occupancy and viewing angle.
All cases preserve the submitted vehicle and boarding geometry, and the E1/E3 close sequences agree with their parent cases' people, components and event order.
E4 changes the recorded stop and route to S2/R2 while retaining the F6 caregiver/stroller operation; other cases retain their default S1/R1 records and assigned modes.

requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

Use the coordinate convention x=0 at the front, positive y toward the boarding side and z=0 at the road. Drawings must respect body sides y=±1100; axle centres x=1400 and 5400; four wheel centres at y=±850, z=325; interior width y=-1000 to 1000; passenger floor x=1800–6500 at z=320; and ceiling z=2700. Preserve the driver-control zone x=250–1750, y=-1000 to 0 and its existing controls. Treat wheelhouses at x=1050–1750 and 5050–5750, side bands y=-1000 to -650 and 650–1000, z=320–700, and the rear service volume x=6500–6850, y=-1000 to 1000, z=320–850 as solid. The main aisle remains x=1800–6500, y=-250 to 500. Locate the landing at x=1900–3100, y=-250 to 1000 and provide doorway height 2100 above the passenger floor. The bridge spans x=1950–3050, deploys from y=1100, z=320 to y=1800, z=300, and fits its stow allowance x=1950–3050, y=350–1100, z=100–300. Door leaves and motion may be designed freely within these constraints. Paired state drawings must show a usable open/deployed arrangement and a credible closed/stowed arrangement. Dimension labels, sections and consistent drawing geometry count as evidence; conflicting geometry or intrusion into required clear regions fails.

Neutral technical plans, elevations and sections are permitted when their intended colourway is identified; they do not need rendered palette fills. This exception does not replace the palette requirements for coloured renderings or swatches.

The process specification must provide a usable upstream record of chassis coordinates and reserved volumes, fixed and tip-up seat use envelopes, N8/F6 labels and passenger counts, doorway/landing/bridge geometry, open/deployed and closed/stowed mechanism states, stopped-vehicle service order, physical controls, support dimensions and contrast, installed fixed copy, route records, and part-to-material assignments. Values must agree with the client fact sheet. Body panels, lining and support finishes require explicit proposed assignments; upholstery and flooring retain their fixed materials. A generic design narrative, unresolved assignments or contradictory records fails. File content establishes the specification's source role; export chronology is not inferred from appearance.

Read a labelled specification for A with base #E8E6DD and accent #1A655E, and B with the same base and accent #655168. Identify body-panel, lining, support-finish, seat-cover and floor assignments that agree with the upstream specification, including recycled PET upholstery and nonslip rubber flooring. State support-to-background LRV difference of at least 30 points. Body and lining material choices, support finishes and accent placement are open, but assignments must remain shared across A/B. Missing codes, an unspecified material category, changed fixed materials or contradictory assignments fails.

The exterior orthographic sheet and each of the two layouts must visibly repeat 4000 mm wheelbase and 1200 mm clear doorway width from the specification. The enlarged plan may use a contextual annotation for the wheelbase. Identify both N8 and F6 on the paired layout, F6 on the turning plan, and the matching single mode on each A/B interior view. Missing annotations, conflicting source values or mode labels inconsistent with depicted tip-up states fail.

Compare the complete vehicle work for unchanged body geometry, wheel size, doorway position, fixed-seat placement and tip-up design across colourways. The paired layout must identify T1/T2, label/count eight N8 and six F6 passenger seats excluding the driver, dimension aisle 750 mm, landing 1200 by 1250 mm and folded projections no greater than 120 mm, and show both door/bridge state pairs. Both layouts must dimension a longitudinal 1000 by 600 mm stroller envelope and separate 500 by 500 mm caregiver envelope. Fixed seats use the prescribed left/right side bands, with two complete envelopes per side within x=3500–5000 and one within x=5800–6500, each at least 700 by 450 mm. Each deployed tip-up occupies a separate 600 by 750 mm envelope within F at x=1800–3500, y=-1000 to -250. The enlarged F6 plan must demonstrate entry, turning and parking without permanent or parked intrusion into the aisle or landing; final stroller/caregiver envelopes remain within F and clear of folded projections. Colour and viewing direction may vary as commissioned; changed geometry, missing dimensions, overlapping parked envelopes or an unexplained seating redesign fails.

Read material annotations and compare visible applications with the specification across both colourways; recycled PET seat fabric, nonslip rubber flooring and the selected panel, lining and support materials must remain assigned to the same parts. Both facilities sheets need matching door/bay sections and installation geometry, located physical STOP buttons, dimensioned 35 mm rails and 38 mm clearance, and an explicit LRV difference of at least 30 points. Show support and retention positions integrated at the actual bay and doorway, with placement evidence and required clear spaces preserved. Place the exit-priority phrase at the door and the folding phrase at the flexible bay in each colourway. Palette changes are allowed; altered equipment positions, missing installed phrases, obstructed clear regions or changed material assignments fails.

E1/E3 must use S1 Library forecourt on R1 in N8; E2 uses the same stop/route in F6; E4 repeats the caregiver/stroller operation at S2 Hall forecourt on R2 in F6. Main case sheets need numbered stationary stages in the prescribed order, with exit clearance before boarding and passage clearance before bridge stowage and door closure. E1 reaches a deployed tip-up through visible support points. E2/E4 begin with T1/T2 folded and show entry, turning and final parking with distinct caregiver space and an unobstructed aisle. E3 places the waiting passenger outside the bridge path. Each E1–E4 sheet must dimension floor 320 mm, curb 300 mm, gap 100 mm and bridge width/reach 1100 by 700 mm, with the correct 20 mm descent and stop landing geometry. The E1 close sequence must follow hand supports to the same seat; the E3 close sequence must clarify the same exit and waiting positions. Close views may crop to their named detail while retaining numbered steps consistent with the parent sequence. Changes in camera scale are allowed; changed components, wrong stop/mode, blocked parking or conflicting event order fails.

Review the entire film and its duration: it must run 12 seconds and include both an exterior observation and E2 caregiver/stroller boarding at S1 Library forecourt on R1. The A vehicle remains stationary in every shot and agrees with the submitted body, F6 seating, installed supports and warm-white/teal palette. T1/T2 are folded before entry. Show waiting, door opening, bridge deployment, exiting passengers clearing, boarding with entry/turning/parking, bridge stowage after passage clears and door closure in that order. Final stroller and caregiver positions remain separate and clear of the aisle. Visible identification and route information must retain the default records. Editing and camera movement are permitted; omitted operations, wrong duration, vehicle motion, inconsistent hardware or boarding before exit clearance fails.
requirementChecks.manualReason: Inspect complete SHA-bound original outputs. This source draft contains no completed professional or model-output review; partial-frame/page sampling cannot prove whole-output compliance.

requirementChecks.criteria: Every image sheet title must contain NEARLINK. Named A renderings use base #E8E6DD with teal #1A655E; named B exterior, interior and facilities renderings use the same base with plum #655168. Other coloured vehicle views default to A. Front and boarding-side identification pairs NEARLINK with three vertically linked open circles and a straight vertical spine wherever those surfaces are visible. Default exterior displays read R1 / MARKET, and interior information reads NEXT STOP / POOL with Library → Pool → Market. E4 must instead visibly carry R2 / GARDENS and NEXT STOP / HALL with Courtyard → Hall → Gardens. Shading and accent placement may vary within the specified palettes; incomplete route strips, incorrect E4 substitutions, swapped colourways or missing identification fails.

The A overview must contain the three required orthographic directions and a front-right perspective. Provide A/B rear-left views, a B front-right view matching the A overview perspective, and A/B dusk views with door closed and bridge stowed. Corresponding A/B viewpoints must permit a direct colourway comparison without disguising geometry changes. All exterior routes remain R1. Finished surfaces, glazing and lamps must express the commissioned contemporary design within the fixed envelope. Different page framing is permitted; missing directions, mismatched comparison angles or incorrect dusk mechanism states fails.

Show each combination of A/B and N8/F6. N8 contains six fixed seats plus deployed T1/T2 and no parked stroller; F6 retains the six fixed seats, folds both tip-ups and occupies the distinct stroller and caregiver spaces while keeping the aisle clear. Compare A/B N8 views at matching viewpoints and A/B F6 views at matching viewpoints and occupied-space arrangements. Colours may change as specified, but geometry, seat design and installation positions must remain consistent. Missing combinations, unoccupied F6 spaces, hidden or contradictory tip-up states, or changed viewpoints that prevent the required comparison fails.

Require at least twelve pages and NEARLINK on the cover. Place wheelbase 4000 mm, doorway width 1200 mm, N8/eight and F6/six passenger-seat records, and complete A #E8E6DD/#1A655E and B #E8E6DD/#655168 codes beside corresponding work. A/B comparisons must use matching viewing angles so palette changes can be assessed against unchanged vehicle geometry. Additional pages and different comparison layouts are permitted; incomplete records, detached facts with no clear association, inconsistent source values or unmatched comparison viewpoints fails.

Verify recognisable reuse from every listed source: specification records, both colourways, all six exteriors, both layouts, all four interiors, both facilities sheets and all six case/detail sheets. Pages may combine, crop or resize sources while preserving identifiable submitted designs and readable relevant content. A source mentioned only in prose, omitted work, illegible token thumbnails or a replacement design that no longer matches the submitted source fails.

The six exterior sheets retain one body and component design, with corresponding A/B viewing angles and unchanged part-to-material assignments. A and B use their specified accents over the shared base, retain R1 identification, and both dusk depictions show the closed/stowed mechanism state.

Both layouts, four interiors and two facilities sheets agree on fixed seating, tip-up geometry, passenger envelopes, doorway/bridge positions and support/control installations. Matching A/B interior and facilities views retain geometry and material assignments while applying the named palette; corresponding mode views preserve the same occupancy and viewing angle.

All cases preserve the submitted vehicle and boarding geometry, and the E1/E3 close sequences agree with their parent cases' people, components and event order. E4 changes the recorded stop and route to S2/R2 while retaining the F6 caregiver/stroller operation; other cases retain their default S1/R1 records and assigned modes.
